findings.affected_surface: Relay SSE backlog-to-live transition and replay cursor
findings.claim: The plan lacks a fixed high-watermark and queue-reconciliation rule, so a message counted in the backlog summary can subsequently be emitted as a live message, violating the promised zero-message summary path.
findings.evidence: The relay subscribes before draining and queues concurrent arrivals. Existing deduplication marks an ID seen only when writeAndMark emits it. The live loop later emits every queued unseen ID. The proposed summary path explicitly skips message writes but does not mark or remove summarized queued IDs. The 10,000-row counting cap also cannot determine the true live edge unless a separate bounded high-watermark algorithm is specified.
findings.repair: Capture an explicit raw-ID high-watermark before the dry-run, constrain counting and summary metadata to rows at or below it, define how newest is obtained when counting stops at 10,001, and discard or mark seen every queued ID at or below that cutoff without stamping delivered_at or inserting grants. Add an interleaving test where a message arrives after subscription but before summary completion.

findings.affected_surface: Peer-agent durable cursor, pendingBacklog state, and presence reminder
findings.claim: The proposed in-memory reminder does not cover the forget-to-pull requirement after restart and is cleared prematurely by a partial poll.
findings.evidence: The plan durably advances the SSE cursor to newest but stores pendingBacklog only in memory. A restart therefore retains the advanced cursor, loses the reminder, and receives no repeated summary. The plan also clears the marker on any poll whose since precedes the old cursor, even though poll_inbox may return only 1 to 1,000 rows and leave most of the summarized backlog unread.
findings.repair: Persist the pending-backlog record together with the advanced cursor, restore it at startup, and update its remaining count and continuation cursor after each poll. Clear it only when the relay reports no remaining summarized rows or the poll cursor reaches the recorded summary cutoff.

findings.affected_surface: Durable task_dispatch delivery and disposition contract
findings.claim: Summarizing task_dispatch messages breaks the existing dispatch contract because the receiver does not get the structured dispatch and the sender interprets absence of a disposition as lost delivery.
findings.evidence: The plan deliberately summarizes task_dispatch and bypasses InboundDispatcher. Current inbound policy explicitly preserves task_dispatch because swallowing it manufactures the same silence used to detect a lost session. The public dispatch tool likewise states that the receiver gets a structured task_dispatch and that silence with no disposition is the lost-session signal.
findings.repair: Make command-bearing task_dispatch rows non-suppressible and deliver them individually, or introduce a protocol-level receipt/disposition that preserves each correlation before advancing past it. Remove the no-kind-split decision unless the dispatch contract is explicitly redesigned and migrated.

findings.affected_surface: Agent-call and switchboard delivery of synthetic backlog summaries
findings.claim: The plan promises a non-envelope, non-replyable summary through agent-call and switchboard, but the current final-mile APIs require an Envelope and always expose its remote message ID; the listed P4 files do not include the components that must change.
findings.evidence: deliverViaAgentCall accepts Envelope and always emits remote_msg_id and kind. Switchboard routing and delivery also accept Envelope, while index routes agent-call delivery through those APIs. Risk judgments: R-a needs a fixed cutoff and bounded live-edge algorithm; R-b needs a separate broadcast field because @team is not a sender; R-c needs a dedicated synthetic final-mile shape; R-d needs an explicit routing choice because the current fallback targets every registration; R-e is acceptable for v1 because the threshold is configurable and zero disables it.
findings.repair: Define a dedicated BacklogNotification final-mile API with no remote_msg_id or reply route, add agent-call-ingress.ts and switchboard.ts to P4, specify authority, retry, cursor-ordering, and switchboard targeting semantics, and test both single-target and switchboard delivery. Use a separate broadcast_count field rather than inserting @team into by_sender.

findings.affected_surface: Cold-start backlog definition and rollout acceptance fixture
findings.claim: The statement that historical @team rows always have delivered_at IS NULL is false because delivered_at is global per message, not per recipient.
findings.evidence: Cold-start fetchPendingSince selects only rows whose delivered_at is null. Any earlier stream presentation calls markDelivered on that shared message row, including @team rows, so a newly registered handle will not necessarily summarize historical broadcasts. Polling differs because fetchInboxSince intentionally ignores delivered_at.
findings.repair: State that cold start applies only to globally undelivered rows and seed such rows explicitly in T5 and rollout validation. If all historical broadcasts must be visible to every newly registered handle, expand the design to per-recipient delivery state instead of relying on delivered_at.

findings.claim: The capped pending_after field is ambiguous at exactly 10,000 because the response does not distinguish an exact count from a truncated count.
findings.evidence: The backlog event explicitly includes pending_capped when its count is truncated, but the poll response specifies only an integer pending_after capped at 10,000. Rendering it as 'K remain' would present a lower bound as an exact total when more than 10,000 deliverable rows remain.
findings.repair: Add pending_after_capped, define pending_after as min(actual, 10000), and render capped values as 'at least 10000 remain'. Test both exact 10,000 and greater-than-10,000 cases using the same ACL and self-exclusion semantics as poll_inbox.

findings.claim: T1 through T12 omit several boundary and integration cases required to detect the identified failures.
findings.evidence: T4 inserts only after the summary and therefore misses the subscribe-to-summary race. T12 expects the marker to disappear after one poll without proving the summarized range was exhausted. There is no test for restart persistence, capped counts, poll ACL filtering, a 200-character presence summary plus suffix, agent-call delivery, or switchboard fanout. T9 covers only claude-channel.
findings.repair: Expand the test matrix with deterministic connect-window interleaving, pending-state restart and multi-page polling, replay_max validation, both 10,000 caps, ACL-filtered pending_after, maximum-length presence summaries, dedicated agent-call summaries, and switchboard routing behavior.
